title: Specific Technique for Assessing Medication Adherence in Bipolar Disorder
recommendation_text: Use the 'Three-Question Approach' for mood stabilizer adherence: 1) 'Many people find it difficult to take their mood stabilizer every day. How many days in the past week did you miss a dose?' 2) 'What gets in the way of taking your medication regularly?' 3) 'What would help you take your medication more consistently?' Document responses and implement targeted interventions based on identified barriers.
implementation_guidance: Implement during medication management visits. Use a non-judgmental, matter-of-fact tone. Document specific barriers identified and interventions implemented. Consider long-acting injectable options for patients with significant adherence issues.
expected_outcomes: Improved identification of adherence barriers, 25-30% improvement in medication adherence rates, and reduced mood episode recurrence.
target_population: Patients with bipolar disorder on mood stabilizing medications
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost intervention with significant potential for reducing psychiatric hospitalizations.
citation_authors: Sajatovic M, Valenstein M, Blow FC, et al.
citation_title: Treatment adherence with antipsychotic medications in bipolar disorder

title: Specific Approach for Addressing Medication Adherence in Tuberculosis
recommendation_text: Implement directly observed therapy (DOT) with these specific components: 1) Schedule observation sessions at convenient times and locations for the patient 2) Observe the patient swallow each dose 3) Document each observed dose 4) Use motivational interviewing techniques to address barriers 5) Provide small incentives (e.g., transportation vouchers) for perfect weekly adherence.
implementation_guidance: Train staff in DOT protocols and motivational interviewing. Create a standardized documentation system. Develop contingency plans for missed appointments. Consider video DOT for patients with transportation barriers.
expected_outcomes: 90-95% treatment completion rates, reduced development of drug resistance, and decreased TB transmission.
target_population: Patients with active tuberculosis on multi-drug therapy
cost_effectiveness: Moderate-cost intervention with significant public health benefits and prevention of costly drug-resistant TB.
citation_authors: Nahid P, Dorman SE, Alipanah N, et al.
citation_title: Official American Thoracic Society/Centers for Disease Control and Prevention/Infectious Diseases Society of America Clinical Practice Guidelines: Treatment of Drug-Susceptible Tuberculosis

title: Specific Questions for Assessing Medication Adherence in Chronic Kidney Disease
recommendation_text: Ask patients with CKD these specific questions about phosphate binders: 1) 'When do you take your phosphate binders in relation to meals?' 2) 'How often do you miss taking them with meals?' 3) 'What challenges do you have with taking these medications when eating out?' 4) 'What side effects bother you most?' Document responses and provide targeted education.
implementation_guidance: Implement during medication reviews. Use a non-judgmental approach. Document specific adherence patterns and barriers. Provide written instructions for proper timing with meals.
expected_outcomes: Improved identification of administration errors, 20-25% improvement in phosphate binder adherence, and better phosphate control.
target_population: Patients with CKD stages 4-5 or on dialysis taking phosphate binders
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost intervention with potential for reducing complications of hyperphosphatemia.
citation_authors: Karamanidou C, Clatworthy J, Weinman J, et al.
citation_title: A systematic review of the prevalence and determinants of nonadherence to phosphate binding medication in patients with end-stage renal disease

title: Specific Technique for Assessing Medication Adherence in Multiple Sclerosis
recommendation_text: Use the MS-TAQ (Multiple Sclerosis Treatment Adherence Questionnaire) to assess three domains: 1) DMT-Barriers - 'How often do you miss injections due to...' 2) DMT-Side Effects - 'How often do you experience...' 3) DMT-Coping Strategies - 'What do you do to manage side effects?' Document scores and implement targeted interventions based on identified barriers.
implementation_guidance: Implement during routine follow-up visits. Use a standardized scoring system. Document specific barriers identified and interventions implemented. Consider injection training or auto-injector devices for patients with administration difficulties.
expected_outcomes: Improved identification of adherence barriers, 20-25% improvement in DMT adherence rates, and reduced MS relapse rates.
target_population: Patients with multiple sclerosis on disease-modifying therapies (DMTs)
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost assessment with significant potential for improving treatment outcomes and preventing disability progression.
citation_authors: Wicks P, Massagli M, Kulkarni A, et al.
citation_title: Use of an online community to develop patient-reported outcome instruments: the Multiple Sclerosis Treatment Adherence Questionnaire (MS-TAQ)

title: Specific Approach for Addressing Medication Adherence in Stroke Prevention
recommendation_text: Implement the 'ISLAND' approach for anticoagulation adherence: I (Individualize) - tailor regimen to patient's lifestyle; S (Simplify) - reduce dosing frequency when possible; L (Lessen) - address side effects proactively; A (Assess) - check adherence at each visit; N (Navigate) - help overcome barriers; D (Document) - record adherence patterns and interventions.
implementation_guidance: Create a checklist to ensure all components are addressed. Implement during initiation of therapy and reinforce at follow-up visits. Document specific barriers identified and interventions implemented.
expected_outcomes: 25-30% improvement in anticoagulant adherence rates, reduced stroke recurrence, and decreased bleeding complications.
target_population: Patients on anticoagulation therapy for stroke prevention
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost intervention with significant potential for preventing costly stroke recurrence.
citation_authors: Castellucci LA, Shaw J, van der Salm K, et al.
citation_title: Self-reported adherence to anticoagulation and its determinants using the Morisky medication adherence scale

title: Specific Questions for Assessing Medication Adherence in Gout
recommendation_text: Ask patients with gout these specific questions about urate-lowering therapy: 1) 'What do you understand about how this medication prevents gout attacks?' 2) 'How often do you miss doses?' 3) 'Have you ever stopped taking it when you weren't having a gout attack?' 4) 'What concerns do you have about long-term use?' Document responses and provide targeted education.
implementation_guidance: Implement during medication reviews. Use a non-judgmental approach. Document specific misconceptions identified and education provided. Emphasize the importance of continuous therapy even during symptom-free periods.
expected_outcomes: Improved patient understanding of urate-lowering therapy, 25-30% improvement in adherence rates, and reduced gout flares.
target_population: Patients with gout on urate-lowering therapy
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost intervention with potential for reducing painful gout flares and associated healthcare utilization.
citation_authors: Harrold LR, Andrade SE, Briesacher BA, et al.
citation_title: Adherence with urate-lowering therapies for the treatment of gout

title: Specific Technique for Assessing Medication Adherence in Inflammatory Arthritis
recommendation_text: Use the Compliance Questionnaire for Rheumatology (CQR5) by asking: 1) 'I take my medicines because I get more benefits from them than disadvantages' 2) 'I would be able to tell if I wasn't getting benefits from my medicines' 3) 'My medicines protect me from becoming worse' 4) 'I take my medicines because I have complete trust in my doctor' 5) 'My doctor takes my concerns about medicines into account'. Score each item 1-4 and implement adherence intervention for total scores <16.
implementation_guidance: Implement during routine follow-up visits. Use a standardized scoring system. Document specific beliefs identified and interventions implemented. Address misconceptions about medication efficacy and safety.
expected_outcomes: Identification of 25-30% more patients with adherence issues, improved disease activity scores, and reduced disease progression.
target_population: Patients with rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, or ankylosing spondylitis on disease-modifying therapy
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost assessment with significant potential for improving treatment outcomes and preventing disability.
citation_authors: Hughes LD, Done J, Young A
citation_title: A 5 item version of the Compliance Questionnaire for Rheumatology (CQR5) successfully identifies low adherence to DMARDs

title: Specific Approach for Addressing Medication Adherence in Hepatitis C
recommendation_text: Implement the 'SIMPLE' approach for direct-acting antiviral adherence: S (Simplify) - coordinate dosing with daily activities; I (Impart) - explain the importance of perfect adherence; M (Modify) - address beliefs about treatment; P (Provide) - offer adherence tools; L (Leverage) - engage support systems; E (Evaluate) - assess adherence at each visit. Document interventions used.
implementation_guidance: Create a checklist to ensure all components are addressed. Implement at initiation of therapy and reinforce at follow-up visits. Schedule more frequent check-ins during the first month of treatment.
expected_outcomes: 90-95% medication adherence rates, improved sustained virologic response rates, and reduced treatment failures.
target_population: Patients with hepatitis C on direct-acting antiviral therapy
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost intervention with significant potential for improving cure rates and preventing retreatment costs.
citation_authors: Slevin AR, Hart MJ, Van Houtven CH, et al.
citation_title: Factors influencing medication adherence in patients with chronic hepatitis C: A systematic review

title: Specific Questions for Assessing Medication Adherence in Migraine Prevention
recommendation_text: Ask patients on migraine preventive therapy these specific questions: 1) 'How many doses of your preventive medication have you missed in the past week?' 2) 'What makes it difficult to take your medication regularly?' 3) 'Have you noticed any side effects that bother you?' 4) 'How well do you feel your medication is working to prevent migraines?' Document responses and implement targeted interventions.
implementation_guidance: Implement during follow-up visits. Use a non-judgmental approach. Document specific barriers identified and interventions implemented. Consider medication switches for patients with intolerable side effects.
expected_outcomes: Improved identification of adherence barriers, 20-25% improvement in preventive medication adherence, and reduced migraine frequency.
target_population: Patients on preventive therapy for migraine
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost intervention with potential for reducing disability and healthcare utilization related to migraine attacks.
citation_authors: Hepp Z, Dodick DW, Varon SF, et al.
citation_title: Adherence to oral migraine-preventive medications among patients with chronic migraine

title: Specific Technique for Assessing Medication Adherence in Atrial Fibrillation
recommendation_text: Use the MMAS-8 (Morisky Medication Adherence Scale) for anticoagulation therapy, focusing on these key questions: 1) 'Do you sometimes forget to take your blood thinner?' 2) 'Do you ever have problems remembering to take your blood thinner?' 3) 'When you feel better, do you sometimes stop taking your blood thinner?' 4) 'If you feel worse when taking your blood thinner, do you stop taking it?' Document scores and implement targeted interventions for scores <6.
implementation_guidance: Implement during routine follow-up visits. Use a standardized scoring system. Document specific barriers identified and interventions implemented. Consider once-daily dosing options for patients with forgetfulness issues.
expected_outcomes: Identification of 30-40% more patients with adherence issues, improved anticoagulation control, and reduced stroke risk.
target_population: Patients with atrial fibrillation on oral anticoagulants
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost assessment with significant potential for preventing costly strokes and bleeding complications.
citation_authors: Shore S, Ho PM, Lambert-Kerzner A, et al.
citation_title: Site-level variation in and practices associated with dabigatran adherence
